BeforeCombatStart.maps_to: no counterpart; on_player_turn_start (letter_opener.py:30-31) is the only reset
BeforeCombatStart.rationale: LetterOpener.cs:87-92 zeroes SkillsPlayedThisTurn at combat start; the sim has no on_combat_start. Combined with the missing AfterCombatEnd this is the sweep's 'reset at a TURN boundary only' bucket (relic/art_of_war shape), and PROMPT.md bug class 13 requires a reader trace before a verdict. Done: the only reader of _skills_this_turn is on_card_played (letter_opener.py:36-37), and turn_structure step 28 opens the play phase AFTER the turn-start hooks, so the turn-1 reset always precedes the first possible read in any combat. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b08.py b08-turn-reset): the same instance carried out of a combat with _skills_this_turn=2 reports 0 at combat 2 turn 1, equal to a freshly-constructed instance. Note this is the mirror of C#'s own arrangement -- C# resets at combat start SO THAT it can skip the turn-1 reset (see AfterSideTurnStart) -- and the sim reaches the same state by always resetting at turn start instead. Rule 7: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json are not hashed by this record.

AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: C#'s player-side AfterSideTurnStart is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 23 -- POST-draw -- and it SKIPS the reset when `PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber == 1` (LetterOpener.cs:100-103) because BeforeCombatStart already did it. The sim resets at on_player_turn_start, which `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` places PRE-draw (step ~18), and with no turn-1 skip. So the sim resets EARLIER than C# and on one more turn -- the opposite direction from relic/kunai, whose C# hook is the pre-block-clear step 9. Unobservable, and the trace is what makes it a divergence rather than a gap: (a) no card can be played between step 18 and step 23, so the extra turn-1 reset writes 0 over 0; (b) the auto-pre-play phase, which is the only turn-start card-playing window, is step 26 -- AFTER both candidate slots -- and the sim's counterpart (MayhemPower, powers.py:3576-3584, on_player_turn_started) likewise runs after on_player_turn_start, so its auto-played Skills are counted on both sides. Contrast relic/kusarigama in this same batch, where the same class of slip IS live because the sim's chosen hook shares a slot with a card-playing power. Rule 7: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json and powers.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): AfterCardPlayed fires once per Replay iteration in C# but once per play in the sim, so a replayed Skill advances the counter by 1 instead of 2
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the hook bracket is per CardPlay now. CombatState._resolve_card_play opens `for play_index in range(play_count)` and fires `hooks.before_card_played` INSIDE it (sts2_rl/combat.py:574-576) and `hooks.on_card_played` at the end of each iteration, gated on the combat still being in progress (sts2_rl/combat.py:597-600) -- CardModel.cs:1904-1965's `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` with Hook.BeforeCardPlayed at :1929 and Hook.AfterCardPlayed at :1957-1959. A replayed card therefore fires both hooks once per iteration, as in the game. WAS: combat.py bracketed the WHOLE play-count loop, so a Throwing-Axe-doubled card fired each hook once.

C# damages `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` -- `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(...)` (src/Core/Combat/CombatState.cs:142; src/Core/Entities/Creatures/Creature.cs:285-299) -- while Relic.living_enemies() filters on `not e.is_gone` only (relics/base.py:294-297). Same mechanism and same verdict as audit/records/relic/bag_of_marbles.json guard G2 (binding rule 3). MILDER HERE than at relic/kusarigama's site, because Letter Opener does not use the set as an RNG population: it iterates it, and DamageCmd.deal itself applies the should_allow_hitting predicate and returns 0 (cmds.py:50-51), so an unhittable enemy simply takes nothing. DORMANT: the ported should_allow_hitting implementers gate on a mid-revival state (IllusionPower powers.py:1572-1575, AdaptablePower powers.py:3372-3375). Porting an effect that makes a living enemy untargetable makes it live only as a difference in hook TRAFFIC (the sim would run the damage pipeline and produce 0), unless the backstop is ever removed. Rule 7: src/Core/Combat/CombatState.cs, src/Core/Entities/Creatures/Creature.cs, relics/base.py, cmds.py and powers.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: C# damages the whole set through ONE multi-target `CreatureCmd.Damage(ctx, HittableEnemies, DamageVar, dealer)` call; the sim loops living_enemies() and calls DamageCmd.deal per enemy
guards.rationale: Checked because a batched multi-target command could plausibly snapshot state or apply damage simultaneously. It does not: the multi-target overload (src/Core/Commands/CreatureCmd.cs) materialises `targets.ToList()`, returns early if the DEALER is dead, then runs the full per-target pipeline in list order inside a foreach -- i.e. sequentially, exactly like the sim's loop. Two narrow differences, both benign here: C# re-checks `originalTarget.IsDead` at the top of each iteration (so an enemy killed by an earlier iteration's on-death effect is skipped) while the sim's list is computed once, and C#'s dead-dealer early-out has no sim analogue. Neither can bite at 5 unpowered damage from a relic with no on-death chaining in ported content; the sim's `self._check_win()` (letter_opener.py:44) closes the combat if the last enemy died, standing in for the CheckWinCondition that follows every C# command (relics/base.py:299-304). Rule 7: src/Core/Commands/CreatureCmd.cs and relics/base.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: DamageVar(5m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (LetterOpener.cs:42) vs DAMAGE = 5 with DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (letter_opener.py:24, 42), and CardsVar(3) vs SKILLS = 3 (letter_opener.py:23)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 5 and 3 are the pinned non-ascension values, and BaseValue (not IntValue) is the read the effect uses -- the same IntValue/BaseValue split relic/brilliant_scarf N2 records as a source idiom. DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED is exactly `ValueProp.UNPOWERED` (valueprops.py:42), so the hit skips Strength/Vulnerable/Weak scaling on both sides (cmds.py:55-58 gates those on is_powered_attack) and is not an 'attack' for on_attacked purposes. `dealer=self.player` mirrors the `base.Owner.Creature` dealer and neither side passes a cardSource. Rule 7: valueprops.py and cmds.py are not hashed by this record.
